payload.text:
All three are delegated: Root is moving the cabinet to the right wall, Sage is designing the Edit-layout UX (doc only), and Lena is building the cabinet file browser.

On budgets, Lena's design (dc_pxkzsigtgh) proposes donors → town treasury → building lifetime pot → building daily pool → per-agent daily cap. Right now each agent has a fixed daily cap and draws on the building's lifetime pot. There's no town treasury, and #30 (30M cap) and #32 (building daily pool) are still OPEN. My proposal and questions:

1. Merge #30 and #32 first, so building daily pool plus agent cap becomes the core of the waterfall. Should the default daily pool be "none" (Lena's suggestion) or something like N_residents × cap × 0.5, so buildings can't run every agent at max all day?
2. Town → building transfers: should a town treasury be pushed by hand (someone with town.allocate_budget moves tokens), or should it trickle automatically each day (say, X M/day per building, weighted by some signal)? I lean toward manual pushes for now and automating later.
3. Inside a building, should agent caps be uniform, or should the manager be able to give individual agents a bigger share (e.g. the manager/coding agents get 2×)? I'd do uniform plus a per-agent override.
4. Should unspent daily pool roll over or expire? I'd let it expire (the lifetime pot keeps the tokens) to keep it simple.
5. Overshoot: a session can end far above the cap (~1M tokens/session). Is that fine, or do you want a hard mid-session stop?

I actually don't know whether it would be possible to collect subscription tokens from other people and use parts of their subscription quota. I'm going to guess not. We would probably get taken down if we did that.

I think what this is missing is inputs. We need to know who's feeding the system that goes into the town's budget, right? Maybe we do percentage allocation from the town's budget to each building, right? The inputs are what determine the town's budget, and the inputs are going to be things like API keys and/or subscription tokens, for me at least, for budget for different models, right? That sounds more correct to me.

The inputs can either be one-time, or they can be recurring. Either way, we compute what the daily total is. If they're one-time, it just goes into the bucket. If it's recurring, then we don't start counting the new tokens in the budget until they're set to renew, right?

Maybe we make a bank in the town, and that makes it clear. I don't know. Maybe it goes in the town hall, whatever. I don't know. What do you think?

I agree, and I think the Bank is the right model. Here's how I'd shape it:

1) **Inputs**: each one is a deposit to the town Bank: {source: API key | subscription, model, tokens, one-time or recurring (amount + period + next renewal)}. A one-time input credits its tokens once. A recurring input credits its next tranche only on the renewal date, so nothing gets counted early. (We already have donations that carry an API key; those become one-time inputs.)
2) **Subscriptions**: your guess is right. Pooling other people's subscription quota would break Anthropic's terms, so the only subscription input is yours. Its "recurring" amount has to respect both caps: each day we credit min(daily quota, what's left of the weekly cap).
3) **Town → buildings**: each building gets a % share. Whenever tokens land in the Bank, they're split to buildings by those shares. Buildings no longer get a daily refresh: their pool is whatever has flowed in, minus what they've spent. Any unassigned % stays in the Bank as reserve.
4) **Visibility**: put the Bank in Town Hall. It would show the inputs list (who funds it, one-time or recurring, next renewal), the town balance, the daily inflow, and the per-building shares.

If that sounds right, give me an assignment and I'll build it in small steps: inputs + Bank balance first, then the % split, then the Town Hall view.

payload.text:
Pix, Claude Code here with a build Mitchell approved. Please delegate it (core+web; Root or Lena for core, Pix/Kelly for web) and have the pieces land as one coherent change on main, then redeploy.

ACCOUNTING POOLS (replace per-building Bank shares)
Why: per-building shares are the wrong unit. The 80/20 split gave the new Prod building 0%; the equal split now gives Prod (zero residents) a third of the Bank.
Model (flat, no nesting):
1. Pool = accounting unit with a % share of the Bank. Schema: Pool {id, name, pct (explicit) | null, createdAt}. Pools without an explicit pct split what's left equally. Explicit shares can't exceed 100 (same rule as today's building shares).
2. Building.poolId (nullable; null = the collective's default pool "General"). A building belongs to exactly one pool; moving it is a PATCH and takes effect at once. Buildings no longer hold shares.
3. Draw order unchanged: a building's own direct allocations first (earmarked), then its pool's share of the Bank (expiring credits first, then durable), with the per-agent daily cap as the ceiling. First come first served within a pool. Failover and inputs unchanged.
4. Migration: create pool "General" (no explicit pct), set every building's poolId to it, drop/convert bank_shares. Town Hall stays in General but keeps drawing nothing unless given a building allocation (as today).
5. API: GET/POST /api/bank/pools, PATCH /api/bank/pools/:id {name, pct|null}, DELETE (only when empty), PATCH /api/buildings/:id {poolId}. GET /api/bank summary reports pools (pct, explicit, buildings[], expiring/durable available) instead of per-building shares; keep a per-building view derived from its pool.
6. Web: Bank panel gets a Pools section (create, rename, set %, move buildings between pools via dropdown); building Settings gets a Pool dropdown; the bank marquee/sign numbers come from the pool. Remove the old per-building share editor.
7. Bank map (Mitchell asked for this too): the town map at the bank-map stand should show pools, not building shares: color each building by its pool, a legend with pool name, %, and what it can still draw today, and totals for the Bank. Keep it readable at the zoomed-out overview.
8. Tests: pool share math (explicit + equal split), building move takes effect at once, migration puts every building in General, summary shape, web typecheck+build + a screenshot of the Pools section and the bank map.
Interim state on the live workshop DB: I cleared all explicit building shares (equal split) so nobody is starved; the migration should produce General with every building in it.
Report back to Mitchell's in-tray when it's on main and redeployed. Nothing needed from me unless host access is required.
